what_its_for: Deflazacort is a corticosteroid (steroid) medicine used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 2 years of age and older. It helps reduce inflammation and slow the loss of muscle strength caused by this condition.
how_to_take: Take deflazacort by mouth once a day, with or without food. If you are using the oral suspension (liquid), shake the bottle well before each use. Use only the measuring syringe provided with your medicine to measure the correct dose. Do not use a household spoon. You may mix the liquid with a small amount of soft food like applesauce or yogurt if needed, but eat or drink the mixture right away — do not save it for later. Swallow tablets whole — do not crush or chew them unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will determine the right dose based on your child's body weight. The usual dose is 0.9 mg per kilogram of body weight taken once daily. Do not change the dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause serious side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose as scheduled. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store deflazacort tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the oral suspension (liquid) at room temperature and use it within 1 month of opening. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet or pour them down the drain unless the label says it is okay. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections, as deflazacort can weaken your immune system and make it harder to fight infections. Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as chickenpox or MMR vaccines) while taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit, as it can increase the amount of this medicine in your blood and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid stopping the medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you or your child experience any of the following: signs of infection such as fever, chills, sore throat, or cough; unusual weight gain or swelling in the face, hands, or feet (moon face or puffy appearance); increased thirst or urination, which may be a sign of high blood sugar; mood changes, depression, or unusual behavior; blurred vision or eye pain; severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, or black/tarry stools; slow growth in children; bone or muscle pain; or if you are exposed to chickenpox or measles. Also tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with deflazacort.
when_it_works: Deflazacort does not cure Duchenne muscular dystrophy, but it can help slow the progression of muscle weakness. Some families notice improvements in muscle strength and function within a few weeks to a few months of starting treatment. It is important to continue taking this medicine as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate changes, as it is working to help protect muscle function over time.
special_populations: Children: Deflazacort is approved for use in children 2 years of age and older. Children taking this medicine should be monitored regularly for growth, bone health, eye problems (such as cataracts), and blood sugar levels. Older Adults: There is limited information on use in older adults with DMD. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of deflazacort during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established. Liver Problems: Patients with liver disease may need dose adjustments, so inform your doctor of any liver conditions before starting this medicine.
